items.title: The injectivity lemma holds over a valuation ring: the module is flat and finitely presented and the map is universally injective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if in Situation labelled situation-mod-injective the ring A is a valuation ring, then the conclusion of the situation holds, namely that the module N is A-flat and of finite presentation over B and that u is universally injective (statement lines 7157-7161; the statement refers back to the situation instead of repeating the three assertions). The proof first recalls that over a valuation ring an A-module is flat exactly when it is torsion free by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-valuation-ring-torsion-free-flat, lets T be the A-torsion of N, notes u(T) = 0 and that N/T is A-flat, hence finitely presented over B by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, so that T is a finite B-module by Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-extension (proof lines 7163-7176). Since N/T is A-flat one has T/m_A T contained in N/m_A N by Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-flat-tor-zero, and the injectivity of the induced map u-bar forces T/m_A T = 0, whence T = 0 by Nakayama's lemma, giving the flatness and finite presentation assertions (proof lines 7178-7184). For universal injectivity the proof invokes Algebra, Theorem labelled algebra-theorem-universally-exact-criteria to reduce to the injectivity of N otimes_A Q -> M otimes_A Q for finitely presented Q, uses More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-generalized-valuation-ring-modules to reduce to Q = A/(a) with a a nonzero element of the maximal ideal, and then takes x in N with u(x) in aM: by Lemma labelled lemma-flat-finite-type-local-valuation-ring-has-content the element x has a content ideal I, which is finitely generated by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-content-finitely-generated and hence principal, say I = (b), because A is a valuation ring; More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-equal-content shows u(x) has the same content ideal, so (b) is contained in (a) by More on Algebra, Definition labelled more-algebra-definition-content-ideal, and x in bN gives x in aN, which is the required injectivity (proof lines 7186-7203). Reducing universal injectivity to a content ideal computation for a principal ideal in a valuation ring is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
